extraction_scope: Source-reviewed worker-6 mechanism ontology record repaired from local XML, PDF text, figure captions, and source-data spreadsheets; no placeholder framework-test claims remain.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AMSIN is best curated as a bacterial cell-wall biosynthesis inhibitor rather than a nonspecific membrane-disruptive peptide.
direct_assay_types: growth-kinetic comparison with antibiotics of known cellular targets

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=9:AMSIN is an inhibitor of bacterial cell-wall biosynthesis

mechanism_claims.adjudication_notes: The source supports cell-wall biosynthesis inhibition through converging kinetics, membrane-permeability, and UMP-accumulation evidence. The record does not promote generic membrane disruption as the primary mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The local source supports the mechanism for AMSIN; it does not independently establish this mechanism for every database-derived synonym or homolog.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AMSIN binds the soluble cell-wall precursor UMP in local CD, ESI-MS, and SPR assays; Lipid II targeting is retained as a source-supported inference from the UMP surrogate system.

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=31:Determination of the binding affinity of AMSIN to UMP by SPR

mechanism_claims.adjudication_notes: The UMP interaction is direct assay evidence. Lipid II targeting is not rewritten as direct Lipid II binding because the local assay used UMP as a soluble surrogate.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct Lipid II binding constants are not extracted from local material; UMP-supported Lipid II targeting remains an inference/caution.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Local source supports low mammalian-cell toxicity, low hemolysis, weak immunomodulatory effects, and no obvious ion-channel activity under tested conditions; these are safety/host-effect context, not an antimicrobial killing mechanism.
direct_assay_types: HL-60 and HEK293 CCK-8 cytotoxicity assay
IL-8 and MCP-1 ELISA cytokine assays
mechanism_claims.adjudication_notes: This claim keeps host-cell and immunomodulation observations separate from antimicrobial mechanism, preventing a direct-mechanism overclaim.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact HEK293 database killing percentages are not promoted because local extractable source data reviewed here primarily supports HL-60 viability and source-text HEK293 method/context.

caution_findings.evidence_context: The paper uses UMP assays as a soluble precursor surrogate; direct Lipid II binding constants are not separately extracted from local material.
